newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian Rosneft oil firm to see equity change soon.
newsitem.headline: Russian Rosneft oil firm to see equity change soon.

text.p: Russia will decide this month how to privatise state-owned oil company NK Rosneft, Itar-Tass news agency quoted State Property Committee chairman Alfred Kokh as saying on Tuesday.
Kokh said a 51 percent controlling stake would remain in state hands, while 23 to 24 percent would go company employees.
The remaining shares -- 25 to 26 percent -- would be sold through an open tender or at a special cash auction, he said.

Rosneft's privatisation has been delayed over quarrels with competitor SIDANKO (Sibirsko-Dalnevostochnaya Neftyanaya Kompaniya) over ownership of crude oil producer Purneftegaz, which now belongs to Rosneft.
The completion of Rosneft's privatisation would nearly bring to a close Moscow's shake-up of its oil sector into privatised companies, most of them vertically integrated.
Rosneft, a holding company, has lost most of its assets through decrees creating separate oil companies.
It is a joint-stock company and is the government's official agent in all oil production-sharing deals.
Rosneft's other leading holdings include the Sakhalinmorneftegaz oil production unit. Its Krasnodar refinery declared bankruptcy in December 1996.
Rosneft boosted 1996 crude oil output to 13.1 million tonnes from 12.8 million tonnes in 1995.
